description: PULL receive path: read one page of the peer messages addressed to the calling session, on demand and without MCP. Takes the caller's own stable agent_session_id; the remaining identity is resolved server-side from that session's live peer_binding row. Returns independently paged direct and role sections. With no direct cursor, entries are the newest messages, newest-first. 'after' is the backward ISO-8601 cursor: it returns rows older than the timestamp and continues with next_after_created_at. 'since' is the first-page forward ISO-8601 horizon: it returns rows strictly newer than the horizon, oldest-first. Continue a forward read by echoing the opaque next_since_cursor as 'since_cursor'; that token preserves the original horizon and last emitted (created_at, id), so equal-timestamp page boundaries are lossless. next_since_created_at is retained only as a compatibility timestamp observation. 'after', 'since', and 'since_cursor' are mutually exclusive. The same fixed forward horizon bounds role_entries, which remain newest-first and page independently through opaque role_after/next_role_cursor. Storing next_role_cursor across sessions would instead resume reading OLDER messages and never surface a new one. role_since_created_at echoes the applied horizon. role_section_status reports computation success, not exhaustion; only next_role_cursor=null means the role section is drained. role_read_coverage explains covered-mark and receipt-hidden rows. Reading role mail here does not itself retire replay insurance; a repeat already read through another path is expected and should be treated as handled. Registered calls return a persisted {job_id, status: queued} admission before the complete operation runs on the messaging owner worker. Read job_service.get_job by that exact job_id until terminal; job.result contains the complete original response envelope, and failures also retain job.error. The receipt reports admission; the operation outcome, full history and readback are in that exact job. Direct Python and direct HTTP callers retain their synchronous operation and response. Do not replay effects after an uncertain terminal write or a lost receipt; reconcile the owned job and actual outcome. Known retained readback limitation: a caller holding more than 100 roles can receive role_section_status=error with query.unbounded_read_over_cap. Inspect role_section_error and role_read_coverage; a queued receipt does not assert complete inbox coverage.
embedding_description: Read the messages other agents have sent to this session, pulling them on demand instead of waiting for a notification. The catch-up read after a restart, a session clear, or a stretch with no live receiver, covering both mail sent to this session directly and mail sent to the roles it holds, one page at a time. Instance pages are complete only when instance_exhausted is true.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: recipient_agent_id and recipient_agent_instance_id, then two sections. entries + next_after_created_at + next_since_created_at + next_since_cursor + instance_exhausted are direct-instance mail. A forward page is oldest-first; next_since_cursor is the opaque lossless continuation and next_since_created_at is only its visible timestamp component. A backward or cursorless page is newest-first. role_entries + next_role_cursor are role mail. role_section_status is 'ok' or 'error' and reports only whether that section computed; role_section_error carries the fault. role_read_coverage reports covered-mark and receipt-hidden counts. Every entry includes thread_id, sender identity and the full message. read_coverage contains JSON-native direct and role objects describing requested/effective boundaries, returned-row endpoints and counts, cursor safety, exhaustion and observer/filter scope; nested role_read_coverage values are lists. Ranges describe returned rows only; unread totals, outside-query rows and human reading remain unknown.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report the two sections separately and say whether each is drained: the instance section only when instance_exhausted is true, the role section only when next_role_cursor is null. Continue a forward direct read with next_since_cursor, never next_since_created_at. Never report role_section_status='ok' as 'no more messages'. Attribute each message to sender_session_label and sender_agent_instance_id. Treat a queued job id as admission only. Retrieve the terminal job before presenting the original operation outcome.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Act on the messages read. For direct mail, fetch pages until instance_exhausted is true, using next_since_cursor for forward continuation or next_after_created_at for backward history. For role mail, continue while next_role_cursor is non-null. Reply to a sender with sender_agent_instance_id and to a role by role name.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Read-only pull of the caller's own peer inbox, plus a liveness touch on the caller's binding. Identity is resolved from the caller's stable agent_session_id via its live peer_binding row; the inbox read itself spans every peer thread targeting that identity and every role the session holds.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: A malformed role_after stays inside the role section fault domain and returns role_section_status='error' while direct entries remain valid. invalid_after means after was not ISO-8601. invalid_since means the first-page horizon was not ISO-8601. invalid_since_cursor means the opaque continuation was malformed or unsupported. peer_inbox_rejected includes combining after, since or since_cursor in contradictory ways. identity_not_registered means no live peer binding matches the supplied session id; that is not an empty inbox. peer_session_ambiguous is a data fault. bridge.not_running means no read happened.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For role_section_status='error', drop role_after and restart only that section. For invalid_after, echo the prior next_after_created_at. For invalid_since, supply an ISO-8601 first-page horizon. For invalid_since_cursor, echo next_since_cursor verbatim rather than constructing or substituting next_since_created_at. Send only one of after, since and since_cursor. Re-arm an unregistered watcher or bridge before retrying identity_not_registered; durable mail remains waiting.

return_value_schema.description: peer_inbox page — the exact shape emitted by peer_inbox_view.serialize_peer_inbox_page (the same payload the localhost /peer/inbox route and the MCP peer_inbox tool return)

next_since_created_at.description: The last returned forward-row timestamp, retained for compatibility and diagnostics; not a lossless page boundary when timestamps tie.

next_since_cursor.description: The opaque tie-safe forward cursor to echo as 'since_cursor'; null unless the request is a forward read with no returned or prior continuation row.

instance_exhausted.description: Whether the instance section is exhausted under the cursor the request used: no older row remains for 'after' (newest-first), no newer row for 'since' (oldest-first).

role_since_created_at.description: The 'since' horizon the role section applied; null when none was requested or the role section failed.

role_read_coverage.description: One {role, covered_mark_present, floor_hidden, receipt_hidden} entry per role the role section read. floor_hidden / receipt_hidden count rows the covered-mark floor / a read receipt hid inside the window this call scanned (counts only, a lower bound on the role's whole hidden history). An entry also carries scan_truncated: true when the receipt refill spent its page budget; its rows are every unserved row found and next_role_cursor continues the scan. Empty when no role is held or the role section failed.

read_coverage.description: JSON-native direct and role section objects: returned-row endpoints/count, requested and effective boundaries, cursor safety and scope; nested role_read_coverage is a list. Outside-query rows, human reading and unread totals are unknown.
